## The same failure through `qwen`, with the mechanism visible

The codex log above shows `write_stdin failed: Unknown process id 0`, which hides *why* the write did
not happen. Running the identical prompt through `qwen` against the same server surfaces the actual
tool results, and they are more damning.

Log: [`direct-qwen.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/runs/direct-qwen.log) ·
formal-ai 0.317.0, qwen-code 0.21.2.

**Both `write_file` calls are rejected, and Formal AI never reacts:**

```json
{"name":"write_file","input":{"file_path":"…/.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino","content":"…"}}
→ {"is_error":true,"content":"File …/general-change-plan.lino has not been read in this session.
    Use the read_file tool first to load the current content … before overwriting it."}

{"name":"write_file","input":{"file_path":"…/hello.txt","content":"exactly: Hello World"}}
→ {"is_error":true,"content":"File …/hello.txt has not been read in this session.
    Use the read_file tool first …"}
```

The harness told it exactly what to do — call `read_file` first — and returned a structured
`is_error: true`. Formal AI called neither `read_file` nor a retry. It went straight to step 3.

**The verification then fails explicitly, with the exit code spelled out:**

```json
{"is_error":true,"content":"Command: cat hello.txt\nOutput: cat: hello.txt: No such file or directory\nExit Code: 1"}
```

**And the turn still ends in success:**

```json
{"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,
 "result":"Completed the general change request for hello.txt and verified it with `cat hello.txt`. …"}
```

Three `is_error: true` tool results in a four-turn session, and the session's own terminal record is
`"subtype":"success","is_error":false`.

### What this adds

1. **The write failure is not codex-specific.** `Unknown process id 0` was a codex-side symptom; the
   underlying behaviour is that Formal AI ignores `is_error: true` tool results entirely. Fixing the
   pid will not fix this.
2. **`is_error: true` is being discarded, not misread.** The error text here is plain English with a
   remedy in it. Any handling of the result at all — even "stop on error" — would have prevented the
   false claim.
3. **Confirms the content-extraction defect concretely:** the content it tried to write to
   `hello.txt` is the literal string `exactly: Hello World`. So even had the write been permitted,
   the file would have held the wrong bytes. That is the same slice reported in §3 of this issue,
   now visible as an actual `write_file` argument rather than only as `expected_evidence`.

### Adjusted suggestion

The fix in §1 above ("fail the step when the capability fails") should be stated more generally:
**treat `is_error: true` on any tool result as a step failure**, and feed the error text back into
the next reasoning step — the harnesses are already returning actionable remedies that are currently
thrown away. A two-turn retry (`read_file` then `write_file`) would have completed this task.
